chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

A man whose sacrificial animal goes astray, then another man finds it and slaughters it—he عليه السلام said: If he slaughtered it in Mina, then it has sufficed on behalf of its owner from whom it had gone astray. But if he slaughtered it in a place other than Mina, it has not sufficed on behalf of its owner.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: it legally sufficed and fulfilled the obligation
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Mina, the prescribed place for this rite
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: its owner, on whose behalf the sacrifice was due
key_terms.فَيَنْحَرُهُ: then he slaughters it as a sacrifice
key_terms.فِي غَيْرِ مِنًى: in a place other than Mina
key_terms.هَدْيُهُ: his sacrificial animal offered for hajj

ai.seo_question: If a lost hajj sacrificial animal is found and slaughtered by someone else, does it count for the original owner?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a lost sacrificial animal for hajj. If another person finds and slaughters it in Mina, it counts for the original owner; if it is slaughtered outside Mina, it does not fulfill the owner's obligation. The narration emphasizes the legal importance of the proper place of sacrifice.
